data.remark:
Exact (a*b) mod p from two trained ReLU cells on a bit-serial loop, running entirely on CPU — tiers 1-9 at 100%, 208 s of the 300 s budget, no GPU required.

Two learned cells (full-adder, full-subtractor) compose an exact modular addition (ripple add plus conditional subtraction), which a fixed radix-2^6 bit-serial Horner loop applies over the raw operand bits: reduce b mod p, then accumulate over the bits of a. The loop feeds operand bits on a fixed, feedback-free schedule and the per-step arithmetic is entirely neural — the deterministic-encoder pattern now instantiated in the official dlp_grokking StreamingDigitReducer reference example.

The CPU result is the point of this entry rather than a limitation: the narrow, sequential operation profile of a bit-serial pipeline is matched to CPU execution, and the same paradigm's GPU-shaped siblings (parallel-prefix and carry-save) are separate entries. Measured across three runs with identical per-tier counts. Cells are trained exhaustively on their complete truth tables and verified exact, so the composed pipeline is exact at any operand width; randomizing the trained weights collapses accuracy to 0%.
